match.reason: The closest bank point, Total interest on a loan, covers how term length affects total interest, but it does not teach combining several debts into one loan, so the consolidation idea is missing.

note:
A fresh check found these problems in this version. Fix each one, and keep everything that is right:
- Card, wording: The example multiplies Sam's old $200 a month by 12 months, but never says the old debts would be paid off in 12 months. Students may think a year of old payments is being compared with the whole 36-month new loan. Say the old debts would be cleared in 12 months.
- Question b, other: The question mostly tests total paid = repayment × number of payments, and the clue spells that rule out. That rule is point 2's idea (loans and repayments). Only the comparison with the $3,000 owed is about consolidation.

rejected.title: Debt consolidation
card: Debt consolidation means combining several debts into one new loan. The new loan pays off the old debts, and you then make one repayment.
It can cut the interest if the new loan has a lower rate than the old debts. It can also lower each repayment.
A lower repayment may mean a longer loan. A longer loan can mean more interest, so the total paid may rise.

Example: Sam pays $120 a month on a credit card and $80 a month on a personal loan, so $200 × 12 months = $2,400. One new loan at $100 a month for 36 months costs $100 × 36 = $3,600, which is $1,200 more.
rejected.remember: Consolidation can give one smaller repayment, but a longer loan may cost more in total.

a.q: Which of these is an example of debt consolidation?
opts: Taking one loan to pay off a car loan and two cards
Getting a new credit card to spend more each month
Paying only the interest on each of three debts
Taking a second loan to buy a newer, bigger car
a.why: Using one new loan to clear the car loan and both cards leaves one debt and one repayment. Paying only the interest keeps all three debts separate. A second loan for a car adds a debt instead of combining them.
a.clue: Count how many debts are left after each choice.

b.q: Omar owes $3,000 in total. He consolidates and pays $150 a month for 30 months. What is his total paid, and how does it compare with the $3,000 owed?
opts: $4,500, which is $1,500 more
$4,500, which is $1,500 less
$450, which is $2,550 less
$3,000, which is the same
b.why: Total paid = $150 × 30 = $4,500. That is $4,500 − $3,000 = $1,500 more than owed. The lower payment is paid over a long time, so the total can rise.
b.clue: Multiply the repayment by the number of payments.

a.q: Lena combines three debts into one new loan. What is debt consolidation?
opts: Paying off several debts with one new loan
Spending more with a new credit card
Paying only the interest on each debt
Borrowing more to buy a bigger item
a.why: Consolidation replaces several debts with a single loan and one repayment. Paying only the interest on each debt does not combine them. Borrowing for a purchase is a different matter.
a.clue: Think of several debts becoming one.
